title: The Kennicutt-Schmidt Law and Gas Scale Height in Luminous and Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies
question: What is the resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt slope at high gas surface density in U/LIRGs, and what do velocity dispersion and surface density imply for the gas scale height, free-fall time and star formation efficiency?

evidence.quote: We adopt the U/LIRG value for the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor (cite: downes1998)
We therefore calculate the star formation rate surface density, $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$, using the thermal-only formula from (cite: murphy2011).

what.value: Arp 220 western nucleus dust contribution of 40%

evidence.quote: the western nucleus of Arp 220, where the dust contributes 40% of the flux (cite: sakamoto2017)

recipe.method: Clean cubes (Briggs robust 0.5), uv continuum subtraction, matched-resolution continuum, smoothing
Moment 0 and 2 with 3 and 4 sigma cutoffs, rebin to beam size, keep S/N>4 pixels
CO to Sigma_mol with Downes & Solomon factor and helium; dust-corrected 93-106 GHz continuum to thermal-only SFR
assumptions: Constant X_CO; no inclination correction; NGC 7469 nucleus excluded

recipe.method: Double power law with free break, bootstrapped 10000 times
H = 0.5 sigma_v^2/(pi G Sigma_mol); rho_mid = Sigma/(2H); t_ff, t_dep, eps_ff per pixel

evidence.quote: We find a slope of $1.74^{+0.09}_{\rm -0.07}$ in the high surface density regime
The mean values range from $150 \pm 15$ pc in NGC 7469 to $190 \pm 20$ pc in NGC 3256.
roughly constant with mean values of 5-7% in each of the 5 galaxies
The velocity dispersions range from 30 km s$^{-1}$ to 160 km s$^{-1}$
